reads: module.json (full graph read node by node; claims section skimmed), sim/misconceived.md, sim/novice.md, sim/misconceived.report.json, sim/novice.report.json. No shell was available, so factory.py validate was not run; G3 was checked by reading every next target and reachability by hand.
gate_note: No G3 or G4 failure found. Every choice target I checked exists, the graph reaches END from S1.gate, and every probe is tap-only.

segments.reason: Airway-first ladder with warning-sign triggers, sure_note on each trap and a clean re-probe at S1.final; the one flaw is that S1.gate_ok offers a skip that bypasses the intubation probe, which is acceptable because S1.final re-tests O1.

Good test ladder with falsely-normal-oximetry model named and re-tested. Weakened by telegraphing: S2.entry's two traps both say 'taken at arrival' and S2.err_step's two traps both start 'Step 3' while the key is the only 'Step 2'. S2.worked packs three ideas into one explain node.

Shock and depth are well modelled, but S3.fluid_ok packs crystalloid, hyperchloraemic acidosis and colloid split into one feedback, S3.depth_ok adds an unrelated erythema message, and the S3.fluid_t8 feedback withholds the answer, so colloid timing is only given by 'Show me why'.

Clean vignettes and a sum check on the adult chart. S4.adult_chart says 'eighteens for the trunk sides and legs' while the chart is anterior and posterior trunk 18 each, a wording muddle that S8.p3_t0 repeats. The child-chart re-test is good.

Parkland arithmetic is strong and the feedback is clear, but the segment is long and repetitive: three sub-probes for one calculation, S5.why re-teaches capillary leak already taught in S3.shock_why, and S5.t1_check has no hint option in the middle of the ladder. The novice path runs 198 steps.

Titration is the strongest management block: hint-free reveal ladders, the direction trap refuted by a counter-case, and a clear child and electrical target split. S6.ambulance's key is the most detailed option, a minor form cue.

S7.spot is broken: two of its three 'trap' orders are the correct orders, and their feedback says 'That is not right. That choice is not right: this order is correct'. A learner holding either wrong model is told they are wrong when they are right. S7.cold_ok packs four claims into one message. S7.b1 and S7.a1 are findable by form.

Good cold consolidation with six unhinted probes that cover the backbone traps, and each wrong option maps to one trap. S8.p2's key repeats the stem's words verbatim, and S8.p12 is a strong clinical decision. The 'That choice is not right.' opener repeats in nearly every S8 feedback.

best_parts: node S1.intub_why: lists the four named triggers (stridor, hoarseness, deep facial or neck burn, soot) and the falling consciousness level, so the warning-sign model is taught as a list the learner can apply.
node S2.why_t13a and S2.why_t13b: each names the wrong model ('falsely normal in carbon monoxide poisoning' and 'the saturation number cannot see it') with a sure_note tied to the favoured exam trap.
node S5.clock_ok: 'burn clock, not the bed clock' is a memorable device with the mechanism (mediators raise permeability from injury), so the clock trap is refuted by cause, not by rule.

node S6.start / S6.start_reveal and S6.elec_ok: the formula-as-estimate probe offers a retry, then a reveal, and the electrical-injury target (75 to 100 mL/h to flush pigment) is taught as an exception to the adult figure.
node S8.p12: a real bedside decision (deep neck burns, calm patient, registrar's 'intubate if voice changes') where each wrong option is a distinct trap (TR30 wait, TR29 numbers first).
node S7.d1 and S7.cold: the escharotomy probe separates depth from the ring with ventilation pressure as the clue, and the cold probe includes an explicit 'no hints' note.
flaws: node S7.spot (and its feedback S7.spot_t0, S7.spot_t1): two of the three 'wrong' labels are correct orders (hydrofluoric calcium gluconate and plastics-smoke hydroxocobalamin). The feedback text 'That is not right. That choice is not right: this order is correct' contradicts itself. Fix: three wrong orders, one correct order, and feedback that names the wrong model.

node S7.a1: the key is the only option with 'alone' and a number, and the only one that is a complete rule; the 'Exam drill' lead-in tells the learner to read the qualifier, so the key is findable by form.
node S7.b1: the key 'Mafenide acetate' is the only option not starting 'Silver'. Telegraph by form. Give the three agents a shared surface (for example, all named by side effect) or vary the stem.
node S2.err_step: two trap options start 'Step 3' and the key is the lone 'Step 2'. A learner who notices that step 3 is the bronchoscopy step eliminates to the key without reasoning about oximetry.
node S2.entry: both traps say 'taken at arrival' and the key does not, so the key is findable by form (DP1).

node S8.p2: the key 'mottled, less painful, with sluggish refill' repeats the stem's own words, so it can be matched by string overlap; and 'Full thickness: slow refill means the burn has no blood supply' is near-dominated, since no one who knows the depth model picks it.
node S7.q3_t1 ('Only the dextrose differs, and the colloid is the same'): dextrose is not in the stem, so the option is dominated and tempts almost no one.
node S7.cold_ok: four correction points in one message (Parkland colloid, Marjolin, mafenide, escharotomy qualifiers) after a four-line quiz. Split into one line per answer.
node S2.worked: three ideas (CO half-life, oximeter blind spot, normal chest film) in one explain message.
node S3.fluid_ok: three messages covering Ringer lactate, hyperchloraemic acidosis and the colloid split; the colloid line is the one the novice lost.
node S3.depth_ok: third message adds 'simple erythema is not counted', an unrelated idea on a depth question.

node S3.fluid_t8: the wrong-answer feedback asks 'when does colloid come in?' and withholds the answer, so the learner needs 'Show me why' to learn the key fact. The misconceived sim notes that it has no sure_note.
node S5.why: re-teaches capillary leak already taught at S3.shock_why; the novice sim reads this as a repeat.
node S5.t1_check: no hint option mid-ladder, unlike its neighbours; a novice is stranded at the one probe where 4 mL versus 2 mL is decided.
node S4.adult_chart: 'eighteens for the trunk sides and legs' does not match the chart's anterior and posterior trunk naming (K4), and S8.p3_t0 repeats the wording.

node S5.t1_try: the key 11,200 mL is the largest of three numbers and the PYQ-keyed figure; the 5,600 distractor is tagged TR3 while the trap map has TR1 as the 11,200 doubling, so the tags and the trap map disagree.

report (report-level, both personas): every fell_recovered and fell_open text opens 'Under pressure' or 'You may have corrected it on the spot', which describes stress the learner did not feel. Within-node corrections are filed under fell_open, so the report does not separate a right-after-feedback correction from an unaided one. All 20 traps recovered on retest for the misconceived persona, yet all 11 objectives read shaky. For the novice, the headline 'weak' overstates the picture (only 5 of 12 cold right, but 21 of 21 guesses right).
merge_ideas: S7.spot rebuilt with three wrong orders (the S7.spot_ok key stays) and the S8.p12 style of feedback: name the wrong model, say why it tempts, then refute.
S6's hint-reveal ladder (retry, then reveal, then a counter-case) applied to S2.err_step and S5.t1_check so every mid-ladder probe has a hint.
The S8 'cold' probes (no hint button) plus a single hinted cold check at the end of S5 would give the report unaided evidence for the Parkland chain, which currently has only S8.p7.

Report: separate 'corrected after feedback' from 'unaided' on each trap, drop 'Under pressure' from the within-node text, and let an all-recovered-on-retest learner read 'secure' or 'shaky' on the basis of the retest, not the first miss.
S3.fluid_t8 and S3.fluid_ok: move the colloid timing into the wrong-answer feedback itself, so the 'Show me why' detour is optional, and keep the feedback to one idea.

misconceived.accurate: Headline 'mixed' and the 'overconfident' calibration match the path; the confident-error list matches the traps held on Sure.
misconceived.inaccurate: All 20 traps were corrected on retest, but all 11 objectives read shaky and the cards tell the learner to revisit the airway, inhalation and TBSA cards as if unfixed. The 'Under pressure' lines describe stress that was not felt.
misconceived.useful: The error-type list and the ordered review cards are useful as a fix list.

novice.accurate: The 'underconfident' call is right: 21 guesses were correct and the learner asked for hints at 9 probes.
novice.inaccurate: The headline 'weak' and the gap readings on O3, O5, O6 and O10 overstate the picture, because within-node corrections are filed as fell_open with no credit for the retry.
novice.useful: The next-step advice (airway card, then the opening segment) is sensible.

note_on_judging: Scores are for teaching quality only; facts were not checked. The module is strong in its trap architecture (20 traps, 39 probes, every wrong option mapped to a trap, hint ladders, sure_notes, fast lanes and cold probes), so the weaknesses are concentrated in S7.spot, the form cues, the packed feedback nodes, and the report's trap-state logic.
